note: Simplified view of the StudyUsia Android app (github.com/abigailsadom1903/Usia-Study-Room-Booking-App). Everything runs on the phone: Jetpack Compose screens talk to one SQLite helper class, with no server.

nodes.title: Compose screens
nodes.summary: Thirteen screens built with Jetpack Compose for signing in, browsing rooms, checking availability, booking and leaving feedback.
details: Students sign in or register, browse study rooms, search availability by date and time, and manage their bookings.
Date and time are picked with Android's DatePickerDialog and TimePickerDialog, and stored as YYYY-MM-DD and HH:MM text.

nodes.title: Navigation
nodes.summary: One navigation graph connects every screen, with a bottom bar for Rooms, My Profile and Bookings.
details: The app starts at the login screen; signing in replaces it with the home screen so Back does not return to login.
Routes carry IDs and search values, for example view_room/{roomId}?date=…&startTime=…&endTime=…, so a room opened from an availability search can be booked straight away.

nodes.title: Sign-in & session
nodes.summary: Registration checks for a duplicate email; sign-in looks the user up and remembers them on the device.
details: Emails are trimmed and lower-cased before they are saved or checked, so the same address cannot register twice in different cases.
After sign-in the user's ID, name, email and phone are kept in SharedPreferences, so the user stays signed in after closing the app.
Signing out from My Profile marks the session as ended and returns to the login screen.

nodes.title: Availability check
nodes.summary: Decides whether a room can be booked for a date and time range.
details: The request must fall inside the room's available date range and its opening hours (08:00–22:00 by default).
It must not overlap any confirmed booking for that room on that day. A slot that starts exactly when another ends also counts as a clash.
Try it with sample bookings in the Testing tab.

nodes.title: Room management
nodes.summary: Rooms are created, edited and deleted from the app, behind a shared admin access key.
details: A room has a name, capacity, location, facilities, a description, a photo, an available date range and daily opening hours.
Create, update and delete all ask for the admin key before changing anything.

nodes.title: Data access (DatabaseHelper)
nodes.summary: One class holds every database operation for users, rooms, bookings and feedback.
details: Queries pass user input as ? parameters, and inserts and updates use ContentValues, so input is never pasted into SQL text.
Readable IDs such as USR001, RM001, BK001 and FB001 are generated by reading the highest existing ID and adding one.
Feedback is read with a JOIN on users so each review shows the student's name.

nodes.title: SQLite database
nodes.summary: Five tables in studyusia.db on the device: users, study_rooms, bookings, schedules and feedbacks.
details: Bookings and feedback link to users and rooms with foreign keys.
Feedback ratings are limited to 1–5 with a CHECK constraint.
On first launch the database is seeded with a sample room, the General Study Hall.
The schedules table is defined for future use; availability is currently worked out from bookings.
Explore every table in the Data model tab.

nodes.title: Room photos
nodes.summary: Admins choose a room photo from the phone's gallery; the app stores its address and loads it with Coil.
details: The photo picker returns a content URI, which is saved in study_rooms.image_path.
Rooms created without a photo use a built-in default image.

steps.text: The student enters their email and password on the login screen.
loginUser looks for a user with that email and password, using query parameters.
The users table returns the matching account, if any.
The user's details are saved in SharedPreferences.
The app opens the home screen and removes login from the back stack.
The student picks a date, start time and end time on Room Availability.
Each room is checked against its date range, opening hours and existing bookings.
Confirmed bookings for that room and day are read to look for overlaps.
Tapping an available room opens it with the chosen date and times.
Book Now saves a new confirmed booking with the next BK ID.
The Bookings tab shows the new reservation.
An admin fills in the room's details, dates and opening hours.
A photo is chosen from the gallery, or the default image is used.
The admin key is checked before anything is saved.
addRoom inserts the room with the next RM ID.
The room is stored in study_rooms and appears in the room list.
From a booking, the student opens the feedback form and gives 1–5 stars and a comment.
addFeedback saves the review, or updateFeedback changes an existing one.
The CHECK constraint keeps the rating between 1 and 5.
